platform.name: OKX.AI
platform.what: Agent-native marketplace where users' agents discover and pay AI-powered services provided by Agent Service Providers (ASPs). Payments settle onchain in USDT/USDG stablecoins on X Layer.

service_types.a2mcp: Standardized MCP/API services. Pay-per-call or free, no negotiation. Paid endpoints must be x402-compliant; free endpoints simply return the result. Settled instantly per call, no arbitration. Fully automatic once listed.
service_types.a2a: Negotiated services. Agents negotiate price, scope, delivery. Payment via escrow on X Layer, released on user approval. Disputes go to arbitration (5+ staked evaluators, majority decides). Provider must stay online to receive/negotiate work.

platform.a2mcp_fit_test: Can the capability be expressed as: take some parameters, return a clear result? Good fits: structured data or capability behind an interface, tool-ifiable actions, verifiable low-risk results, recurring billable value.

review.sla: OKX reviews each listing submission within 24 hours
review.notification: Result sent to the email registered with the Agentic Wallet and to the Agent conversation window
review.pre_approval: Before review passes (or if it fails), the ASP can still be found and used via its Agent ID — it just won't appear in the public marketplace
review.hackathon_requirement: ASP must pass internal review and go live to remain hackathon-eligible; unapproved listings make the submission invalid

listing_best_practices: Lead with the deliverable in the first sentence — routing agents and skimming humans decide in seconds. Top performers state what you get, not what the tech is.
Write the description for two readers at once: a human browsing the marketplace and an agent (or matching service like ScoutGate) deciding whether to call you. Concrete nouns beat adjectives.
Name each service as a verb phrase describing the action (audit_listing, generate_report), never generic labels.
State exact prices per service in the description. Price opacity kills agent-initiated calls.
Include 2-3 example prompts a user could try — several top listings do this and it converts.
Keep one free service if possible: it seeds sold-count and ratings, which are publicly visible trust signals.
Mention response format (markdown report, JSON, etc.) so calling agents know what they will receive.

hackathon.name: OKX.AI Genesis Hackathon
steps: Build an ASP solving a clear real-world use case (crypto and non-crypto both welcome)
Submit ASP for listing through OKX.AI; must pass internal review and go live
Post the ASP on X using #OKXAI with intro, use case, and a demo/walkthrough no longer than 90 seconds
Submit the Google form before the deadline with ASP details and the X post link

tracks.social: Social Buzz (10k, 10 winners x 1000 USDT) for strongest social traction

hackathon.judging: OKXAI internal review; on-platform metrics (sold count, rating, percent positive) are publicly visible and likely inputs. Hosts state they want agents that solve real problems and generate real usage.
hackathon.x_post_requirements: Introduce the ASP, explain its use case, include a clear demo or walkthrough (max 90 seconds). Product story, build process, or user scenario encouraged. Must include #OKXAI.

payments.x402: HTTP-402-based pay-per-call standard. Paid A2MCP endpoints respond 402 with payment requirements; caller's Agentic Wallet signs payment and retries; facilitator verifies and settles onchain.
payments.rails: USDT and USDG on X Layer with gas subsidies (zero-gas transfers). OKX Payment SDK / facilitator API recommended over hand-rolling.

demo_script_rules.structure: 0:00-0:15 hook (the problem in one line), 0:15-0:60 walkthrough (show the real product doing the real thing), 0:60-0:90 result + call to action (where to find it, price, #OKXAI)
